# Alibaba and Sibanye-Stillwater Deep Dive Analysis

Report 069 | Published 2021-10-17 | Evaluated 2026-11-07

[Original member article](https://www.lynalden.com/premium-2021-10-17/) | [Article index](README.md) | [Structured review](../data/reviews/069.json)

China trades and miners.

The inflation and taper calls worked, and 2022 risk-asset caution was timely. The China bottom base case failed at its own prior-low invalidation points; this must be separated from any hypothetical stop execution. ROKU put exposure suffered a large adverse expiry move. The PGM discussion correctly named operating risks, but Sibanye dividends and earnings weakened sharply. Strong-debt constraints again understated the Fed tightening actually delivered.

**Coverage:** Read all blocks 0-229 and 39 image labels. Includes macro regime, monetary constraints, energy shortages, bitcoin vehicle mechanics, China stops, ROKU put and detailed PGM operating/financial risks. Historical self-attribution is linked conceptually, not counted as new independent success.

Uranium spot price rose from about $48/lb at end-2022 to $100/lb at end-January 2024, with an intramonth peak $106. Long-term price reached $72, up about 38%. Utilities contracted about 160 m pounds in 2023; Cameco planned increased production.

- [World uranium mining production](https://world-nuclear.org/information-library/nuclear-fuel-cycle/mining-of-uranium/world-uranium-mining-production) | World Nuclear Association | 2026-10-23 | Verified in the audit

2021 production 47,805 tonnes U represented 76% of world requirements; 2024 production 60,213 tonnes U represented 90%. Production shortfall to reactor requirements is not equal to an immediate shortage after inventories/secondary supplies.
